Statement 2 is a fair, if compressed, description: the mansab was a numerical rank (zat/sawar) from which an officer's pay and status followed, so treating it as a ranking system governing salary is acceptable. Answer 1 and 2 only.]

stem: The Planning Commission was established in the year
solution: The Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution in March 1950, with the Prime Minister as its ex-officio chairman; it was neither a constitutional nor a statutory body, which is why it could be replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015 without an amendment. The First Five Year Plan followed in 1951. Matches option C.
subject: Economics
subtopic: Five Year Plans and Indian Planning

stem: The very first five-year plan of India was based on the model of:
reviewNote: KEY DISPUTE: printed key is (A) Mahalanobis model. The FIRST Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, option (B); the Mahalanobis model underpinned the SECOND plan. Printed key retained.
solution: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was built on the Harrod-Domar framework, which makes the growth rate the savings rate divided by the capital-output ratio, and it accordingly concentrated on agriculture, irrigation and power. The Mahalanobis model is the tempting distractor because it is the more famous Indian model, but it belongs to the Second Plan (1956-61) and its heavy-industry strategy. The Bombay Plan of 1944 was an industrialists' proposal and was never the basis of a Plan. Matches option B.
subject: Economics
subtopic: Five Year Plans and Indian Planning

stem: Which of the following pair is not correctly matched?
optA: Total area of India - 3.28 million sq. km
solution: India's area is about 3.28 million square kilometres, its mainland runs from \(8^{\circ}4'\)N to \(37^{\circ}6'\)N and from \(68^{\circ}7'\)E to \(97^{\circ}25'\)E, so those three pairs are the standard textbook figures and are correctly matched. The count of states is the odd one out: since the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir on 31 October 2019 India has had 28 states and 8 Union Territories, so the figure of 29 is out of date. Matches option D.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India

stem: Which of the following rivers of India crosses the tropic of cancer twice?
solution: The Mahi rises in Madhya Pradesh, flows north into Rajasthan, then swings west and south-west through Gujarat to the Gulf of Khambhat. That hairpin course carries it over the Tropic of Cancer once on the way north and again on the way back south, which no other Indian river does. The Chambal stays north of the Tropic throughout and the Narmada runs well to the south of it, so neither crosses it even once. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies

stem: Which one of the following statements about the Indian desert is/are correct?
optA: The Indian desert lies towards the western margins of the Arvali Hills
optB: This region receives very low rainfall below 150 mm per year
optC: Luni is the only large river in this region
solution: The Thar does lie along the western margin of the Aravalis, it does receive under 150 mm of rain in a year, and the Luni is indeed the only large river of the region - these are the three standard descriptors of the Indian desert. Since each individual statement is accurate, the combined choice is the one to take. Matches option D.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India

stem:
Consider the following relief features --
1. Zaskar Range
2. Dhauladhar Range
3. Ladakh Range
4. Karakoram Range
The correct south to the northward sequence of the above relief features is
solution: Working northward from the plains, the Dhauladhar belongs to the Lesser Himalaya and comes first. Beyond the Great Himalaya lies the Zaskar range, then the Ladakh range, and the Karakoram is the outermost northern wall, the one carrying K2. The order is therefore Dhauladhar, Zaskar, Ladakh, Karakoram. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India

stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
optA: The Western Ghats are relatively high in their Northern region.
optB: The Anaimudi is the highest peak in the Western Ghats.
optC: Tapti river lies to the south of Satpura.
optD: The Narmada and the Tapti river valleys are said to be old rift valleys
solution: The Western Ghats gain height from north to south, and the tallest peaks - Anaimudi at 2695 m and Doda Betta - all lie in the southern section, so the claim that they are relatively high in their northern region is the incorrect one. Anaimudi being the highest peak of the range is correct, the Tapti does flow south of the Satpura while the Narmada flows to its north, and both valleys are recognised as old rift valleys. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India

stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The Barren Island volcano is an active volcano located in the Indian territory.
2. Barren Island lies about 140 km east of Great Nicobar.
3. The last time the Barren Island Volcano erupted was in 1991 and it has remained inactive since then.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Barren Island in the Andamans is India's only confirmed active volcano, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 misplaces it: it lies roughly 138 km north-east of Port Blair, not east of Great Nicobar, which is hundreds of kilometres further south. Statement 3 is wrong as well, because after the 1991 eruption the volcano has erupted repeatedly, including in 1994-95, 2005, 2017 and 2018, so it has not lain dormant. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time

stem: Toda Tribe is the inhabitant of :
solution: The Toda are a small pastoral community of the Nilgiri plateau in Tamil Nadu, known for buffalo herding, barrel-vaulted huts and the temple-dairy at the centre of their ritual life. Matches option C.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India

stem:
Assertion (A) : Yamuna becomes a dead river between Delhi and Agra most of the year.
Reason (B) : Yamuna is a non-perennial river.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
optA: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
optB: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
reviewNote: [BROKEN-STEM: Printed defect: the stem labels the second proposition Reason (B) while all four choices refer to it as (R). Cosmetic only - the question is answerable exactly as printed and the answer is unaffected. Left as printed.]
solution: The assertion is accepted: downstream of the Wazirabad barrage almost the entire flow is drawn off for irrigation and water supply while untreated sewage enters, so the Delhi-to-Agra stretch carries very little dissolved oxygen for most of the year and is routinely described as ecologically dead. The reason offered is false - the Yamuna rises at the Yamunotri glacier and is fed by snowmelt, which makes it a perennial Himalayan river; its dry-season emptiness below Delhi is caused by abstraction and pollution, not by the river failing at source. So a true assertion is paired here with a false reason. Matches option C.
subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies

stem: The Indian monsoon is indicated by seasonal displacement because of
optA: Differential temperature of land and sea
solution: The monsoon is a seasonal reversal of wind driven by the fact that land heats and cools far faster than the sea. In summer the intensely heated north-western plains form a low-pressure trough that draws moist air in from the ocean, and in winter the cold high over the land pushes air back out to sea. Cold Central Asian air shapes the winter regime but does not create the seasonal displacement, and similarity of temperature would destroy the pressure gradient that drives the whole system. Matches option A.
subject: Geography

stem: Sargasso Sea is related to the Ocean, that ocean is --
solution: The Sargasso Sea is the calm, weed-covered centre of the North Atlantic gyre, ringed by the Gulf Stream, the North Atlantic Drift, the Canary Current and the North Equatorial Current. That current ring is why it is the only sea on Earth with water boundaries instead of coasts. Matches option B.
subject: Geography

stem: Which of the following is a warm current?
solution: The Brazil Current carries warm equatorial water southward along the eastern coast of South America, so it is the warm one here. The Falkland Current flows north out of the Southern Ocean, the Labrador Current brings polar water and icebergs south past Newfoundland, and the Canary Current is a cool eastern-boundary current off north-west Africa - all three are cold. Matches option B.
subject: Geography

stem: Which strait connects the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean?
solution: Bab-el-Mandeb, between Djibouti and Yemen, joins the southern end of the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and so to the Indian Ocean; with the Suez Canal at the other end it completes the Europe-to-Asia sea route. Hormuz links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, the Bosphorus joins the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, and Malacca separates Sumatra from the Malay Peninsula. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies

stem: 'Great Barrier Reef ' is---
optD: A range of the Rocky Mountains
solution: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world, running about 2300 km along the Queensland coast in the Coral Sea off north-eastern Australia, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Matches option A.
subject: Geography

stem:
Arrange the following atmospheric zones in terms of the distance from the earth's surface in increasing order and select the correct answer from the codes given below:
1. Thermosphere
2. Troposphere
4. Mesosphere
3. Stratosphere
Code :
reviewNote: [BROKEN-STEM: Printed defect: the numbered list is set out of order as 1, 2, 4, 3. Each name still carries its own number, so the mapping is unambiguous and the question is answerable as printed. Left as printed.]
solution: Measured upward from the surface the layers run troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere - the ozone layer sits in the stratosphere and meteors burn up in the mesosphere. Reading off the number attached to each name, that order is 2, 3, 4, 1. The trap is the sequence that puts the thermosphere third, ahead of the mesosphere, which reverses the outermost two layers. Matches option D.
subject: Geography

stem: A sudden fall of Mercury in Barometer indicates;
solution: The barometer measures atmospheric pressure, and a sudden fall means a deep low-pressure system is arriving. Air rushes in towards the low and rises, and the rising moist air condenses, giving cloud, rain and strong wind. Fair settled weather is signalled instead by a steady or slowly rising mercury column, and the instrument says nothing directly about how hot or cold it will be. Matches option B.
subject: Geography

stem: The headquarter of the International Maritime Organization is located at:
solution: The International Maritime Organization, the United Nations agency responsible for the safety and security of shipping and for preventing marine pollution from ships, has its headquarters on the Albert Embankment in London. Geneva hosts the World Health Organization and the International Labour Organization, Paris hosts UNESCO, and Rome hosts the Food and Agriculture Organization. Matches option A.
subject: Polity
chapter: World Polity, Democracy and International Relations

stem: Which of the following will contain same number of atoms as 20 g of calcium?
solution: 20 g of calcium is \(20/40 = 0.5\) mol, that is half of Avogadro's number of atoms. Oxygen gas is diatomic, so 8 g is \(8/32 = 0.25\) mol of \(O_{2}\) molecules and therefore \(0.5\) mol of oxygen atoms - the same atom count. The trap is 16 g of oxygen gas, which is 0.5 mol of molecules but a full mole of atoms, while 24 g of magnesium and 12 g of carbon are each a full mole of atoms as well. Matches option C.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Mole Concept, Avogadro's Law and Molar Calculations

stem: A device used for measurement of radioactivity is
solution: The Geiger-Muller counter detects ionising radiation: an entering particle ionises the gas in the tube, the high voltage multiplies that into an avalanche, and each resulting pulse is counted. The mass spectrometer separates ions by mass-to-charge ratio, a cyclotron accelerates charged particles and a nuclear reactor generates energy, so none of those measures activity. Matches option D.
subject: Physics

stem: Molten sodium chloride conducts electricity due to the presence of
solution: Sodium chloride is ionic, and in the solid its ions are locked in the lattice. Melting frees the sodium and chloride ions to move, and it is this migration of ions towards the electrodes that carries the current - which is also why the molten salt is decomposed rather than merely heated. Metals conduct through free electrons, but an ionic melt has none available. Matches option B.
subject: Chemistry

stem: Balmer series in hydrogen spectrum appears in
solution: The Balmer series is the set of hydrogen transitions that end on the \(n = 2\) level, and the photon energies involved put its lines between about 656 nm and 365 nm, so its prominent members fall inside the visible band. The Lyman series, ending on \(n = 1\), is ultraviolet, while the Paschen and Brackett series, ending on \(n = 3\) and \(n = 4\), lie in the infrared. Matches option B.
subject: Physics

stem: In Rutherford experiment of discovery of nucleus, when thin foils of metal were bombarded with a beam of \(\alpha\)-particle
optA: most of the alpha particles pass through the metal foil without any deflection
optB: all the the alpha particles pass through the metal foil
optC: most of the alpha particles are deflected through small angles
optD: most of the alpha particles are deflected back
reviewNote: Source typo: option (B) reads 'all the the alpha particles'.
solution: In the gold-foil experiment the overwhelming majority of \(\alpha\)-particles went straight through undeflected, and that is precisely what told Rutherford the atom is mostly empty space. Only a small fraction were deflected appreciably and about one in twenty thousand bounced back, and it is that rare large-angle scattering that revealed the tiny dense nucleus. Saying all passed through would leave the nucleus undiscovered, and saying most were deflected would imply a solid atom. Matches option A.
subject: Chemistry

stem: Select the correct statement from the following
optA: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin
optB: Brass in an alloy of copper and aluminium
optD: Stainless steel is chromium plated iron
solution: Bronze is copper alloyed with tin, and that is the only correct pairing offered. Brass is copper with zinc, not aluminium; German silver is a copper-zinc-nickel alloy containing no silver at all despite its name; and stainless steel is a true alloy of iron with chromium and nickel throughout its bulk, not iron carrying a chromium coating. Matches option A.
subject: Chemistry

stem: Electrical conductivity of metal decreases
solution: Current in a metal is carried by free electrons, and raising the temperature makes the lattice ions vibrate more violently, so the electrons collide more often and drift less freely. Resistivity therefore rises with temperature and conductivity falls. Cooling has the opposite effect, which is why conductors are so much better at cryogenic temperatures. Matches option B.
subject: Physics

stem: Kirchhoff's current law is based on
solution: The junction rule says the total current entering a node equals the total current leaving it, which is simply a statement that charge does not accumulate at a junction. It therefore rests on conservation of charge. It is the loop rule, dealing with potential differences round a closed path, that expresses conservation of energy. Matches option D.
subject: Physics

stem: The dimensions of heat capacity are
solution: Heat capacity is the heat needed per unit rise in temperature, so its dimensions are those of energy divided by temperature. Energy is \(\left\lbrack ML^{2}T^{-2} \right\rbrack\), and dividing by \(\left\lbrack K \right\rbrack\) gives \(\left\lbrack ML^{2}T^{-2}K^{-1} \right\rbrack\). Note that this is heat capacity, not specific heat capacity, so no mass appears in the denominator. Matches option D.
subject: Physics

stem: A black body is at a temperature of 500 K. It emits energy at a rate which is proportional to
reviewNote: [KEY CORRECTED D -> A. Two independent blind derivations, neither with sight of the key nor of the other, reached the same answer against it. This is publisher practice material, not a past paper, so there is no issued key to preserve; the book prints D. Basis: Stefan-Boltzmann law: emissive power E = sigma*T^4, so at T = 500 K the rate is proportional to (500)^4. For a black body the total energy radiated per unit area per unit time is E = sigma*T^4 (Stefan-Boltzmann), with T the absolute temperature. T = 500 K is already absolute, so the rate is proportional to (500)^4 directly. Options B, C and D correspond to no radiation law.]
solution: Stefan's law states that the power radiated by a black body varies as the fourth power of its absolute temperature, \(E = \sigma T^{4}\). At 500 K the emission rate is therefore proportional to \((500)^{4}\). Each of the lower powers would describe a far weaker temperature dependence than a radiating body actually shows. Matches option A.
subject: Physics

stem: \(n\) equal resistors are first connected in series and then connected in parallel. What is the ratio of the maximum resistance to the minimum resistance?
reviewNote: [KEY CORRECTED A -> C. Two independent blind derivations, neither with sight of the key nor of the other, reached the same answer against it. This is publisher practice material, not a past paper, so there is no issued key to preserve; the book prints A. Basis: Ratio = n^2. Series gives the maximum nR; parallel gives the minimum R/n; (nR)/(R/n) = n^2. For n identical resistors each of resistance R: series combination R_s = nR, and this is the largest resistance obtainable. Parallel combination 1/R_p = n/R, so R_p = R/n, the smallest. Ratio R_max/R_min = nR / (R/n) = n^2. R cancels, so the answer is dimensionless in n as required. Sanity check with n = 2, R = 6: series 12, parallel 3, ratio 4 = 2^2.]
solution: In series the n resistors simply add, giving \(nR\), which is the largest value the set can produce. In parallel they give \(R/n\), the smallest. The ratio of maximum to minimum is \(nR \div (R/n) = n^{2}\), and note that R cancels, so the answer depends only on how many resistors there are. The trap is quoting n itself, which is the ratio of either arrangement to a single resistor rather than of the two arrangements to each other. Matches option C.
subject: Physics

stem: The ratio of the dimension of Planck's constant and that of the moment of inertia is he dimension of
reviewNote: [KEY CORRECTED B -> A. Two independent blind derivations, neither with sight of the key nor of the other, reached the same answer against it. This is publisher practice material, not a past paper, so there is no issued key to preserve; the book prints B. Basis: [h]/[I] = (M L^2 T^-1)/(M L^2) = T^-1, the dimension of frequency. Planck's constant from E = h*nu gives [h] = [E]/[nu] = (M L^2 T^-2)/(T^-1) = M L^2 T^-1 (equivalently it is the dimension of angular momentum). Moment of inertia I = sum(m r^2) has [I] = M L^2. Dividing: M and L^2 cancel, leaving T^-1. That is frequency. Velocity would be L T^-1, acceleration L T^-2, time T - none matches.]
solution: Planck's constant has the dimensions of action, that is energy multiplied by time, \(\left\lbrack ML^{2}T^{-1} \right\rbrack\), the same as angular momentum. Moment of inertia is \(\left\lbrack ML^{2} \right\rbrack\). Dividing one by the other leaves \(\left\lbrack T^{-1} \right\rbrack\), which is frequency. Matches option A.
subject: Physics

stem: A bullet of mass 2 gm is having a charge of \(2\mu C\). Through what potential difference must it be accelerated, starting from rest, to acquire a speed of 10 m/s?
solution: The work done by the accelerating field becomes kinetic energy, so \(qV = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\). With \(m = 2 \times 10^{-3}\) kg and \(v = 10\) m/s the kinetic energy is 0.1 J, and dividing by a charge of \(2 \times 10^{-6}\) coulomb gives \(V = 5 \times 10^{4}\) V, that is 50 kV. The large figure is not a slip: two microcoulombs is a very small charge, so a big potential difference is needed to give a two-gram bullet even a modest speed. Matches option C.
subject: Physics

stem: Three resistances each of 4\(\Omega\) are connected to form triangle. The resistance between any two terminals is
solution: Take any two corners of the triangle. The single resistor joining them, \(4\ \Omega\), is in parallel with the path round through the third corner, which is two resistors in series and so \(8\ \Omega\). The parallel combination is \((4 \times 8)/(4 + 8) = 8/3\ \Omega\). Adding all three in series to get \(12\ \Omega\) is the standard error, and it ignores the fact that the network offers two routes between the terminals. Matches option D.
subject: Physics

stem: Bernoulli's theorem is based upon
solution: Bernoulli's theorem says that for steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow the sum of pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy per unit volume stays constant along a streamline. That is the work-energy theorem applied to a fluid element, so the principle underneath it is conservation of energy. Conservation of mass is what the equation of continuity expresses, and the two are often confused. Matches option B.
subject: Physics
chapter: Fluid Mechanics and Properties of Matter

stem: An iron needle floats on the surface of water. This phenomenon is attributed to:
solution: Iron is roughly eight times as dense as water, so buoyancy alone cannot hold the needle up. What supports it is surface tension: the water surface behaves like a stretched membrane, and where the needle depresses it the inclined surface forces acquire upward vertical components that balance the weight. Adding a little detergent lowers the surface tension and the needle sinks at once, which is the classroom demonstration of exactly this point. Matches option C.
subject: Physics
chapter: Fluid Mechanics and Properties of Matter

stem: Chemical formula of borax (Sodium tetraborate) is
solution: Borax is sodium tetraborate decahydrate, \(Na_{2}B_{4}O_{7}.10H_{2}O\), carrying ten molecules of water of crystallisation. That is why it first swells and loses water on heating before fusing to the clear glassy bead used in the borax bead test. The anhydrous salt and the lower hydrates do exist, but the name borax refers to the decahydrate. Matches option C.
subject: Chemistry

stem: A moving body is covering distances in proportion to the square of time. The acceleration of the body is
reviewNote: Source artefact: printed as 'pro-portion' across a line break; de-hyphenated to 'proportion'.
solution: If the distance covered varies as the square of time then \(s = kt^{2}\). Differentiating once gives \(v = 2kt\) and differentiating again gives \(a = 2k\), which is a constant. Put the other way round, \(s \propto t^{2}\) is precisely the signature of uniformly accelerated motion starting from rest. Matches option D.
subject: Physics

stem: The focal length of a convex lens as \(f\). It makes imaginary image of size n times that of an object. The distance of the object from the lens is
reviewNote: [BROKEN-STEM: Printed defect: the fourth option is malformed as \(\frac{(n+1)}{f}f\), which reduces to \(n+1\) and is not even a length. It is a distractor, not the answer, so the question is still answerable - the correct option is intact. Left as printed.]
solution: Only when the object lies inside the focal length does a convex lens form a virtual image, and that image is erect and magnified, so \(m = v/u = n\). Substituting \(v = nu\) into \(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\) gives \(\frac{1 - n}{nu} = \frac{1}{f}\), so the object distance has magnitude \(\frac{(n-1)f}{n}\). Checking with \(n = 2\) and \(f = 10\) cm, an object at 5 cm gives \(v = -10\) cm, a virtual image twice the size, as required; the \((n+1)\) form instead puts the object outside the focal length and yields a real inverted image. Matches option C.
subject: Physics

stem: The purest form of Fe is
solution: Wrought iron is the purest commercial form of iron, about 99.5 per cent Fe with only a trace of carbon left after the carbon and slag have been driven off. Cast iron carries 2 to 4 per cent carbon and ordinary steel 0.2 to 2 per cent, while stainless steel is deliberately alloyed with chromium and nickel, so all three are less pure than wrought iron. Matches option D.
subject: Chemistry

stem: According to which law CO and CO\(_{2}\) are formed?
solution: Carbon combines with oxygen in two different ratios: in \(CO\) a fixed 12 g of carbon takes 16 g of oxygen, while in \(CO_{2}\) the same 12 g takes 32 g. The two oxygen masses stand in the simple whole-number ratio 16:32, that is 1:2, and this is exactly what the law of multiple proportions asserts. The law of constant proportions describes a single compound of fixed composition, so it cannot account for two different oxides of the same pair of elements. Matches option C.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Stoichiometry and Laws of Chemical Combination

stem: The neutron was discovered by.
reviewNote: Source typo: the stem ends 'discovered by.' with a stray full stop.
solution: James Chadwick identified the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with \(\alpha\)-particles and showing that the penetrating radiation given off had to be an uncharged particle of roughly the proton's mass. Rutherford had predicted such a particle and is credited with the proton and the nuclear model, Goldstein found the anode or canal rays, and Moseley's X-ray work established the concept of atomic number. Matches option C.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Atomic Number, Mass Number and Subatomic Particles

stem: Which of the following oxides is acidic?
solution: Non-metal oxides are acidic, and \(SO_{2}\) dissolves in water to give sulphurous acid, turning moist blue litmus red. \(Na_{2}O\) is a metal oxide and strongly basic, dissolving to give sodium hydroxide, while \(Al_{2}O_{3}\) is amphoteric and reacts with both acids and alkalis rather than behaving as an acid alone. Matches option C.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes

stem: The large energy released in atomic bomb explosion is due to
optC: conversion of heavy atoms to lighter atoms
solution: In fission the total mass of the fragments and the released neutrons is slightly less than the mass of the original nucleus, and that missing mass appears as energy through \(E = mc^{2}\). Because \(c^{2}\) is so enormous, a very small mass defect liberates a very large amount of energy. The neutrons released matter because they sustain the chain reaction, but they are not themselves the source of the energy. Matches option B.
subject: Physics

stem: Which of the following is amphoteric?
solution: Zinc oxide is amphoteric: with acids it gives zinc salts and water, and with sodium hydroxide it gives sodium zincate. \(Li_{2}O\) is a basic metal oxide and \(SO_{2}\) is an acidic non-metal oxide, so each of those reacts with only one of the two classes of reagent. Matches option B.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes

stem: The energy equivalent to 1 kilogram of matter is about
solution: By mass-energy equivalence \(E = mc^{2} = 1 \times (3 \times 10^{8})^{2} = 9 \times 10^{16}\) J. To the nearest order of magnitude among those offered, that is \(10^{17}\) J. Matches option C.
subject: Physics
reviewNote: [KEY CORRECTED D -> C. Two independent blind derivations, neither with sight of the key nor of the other, reached the same answer against it. This is publisher practice material, not a past paper, so there is no issued key to preserve; the book prints D. Basis: E = mc^2 = 1 kg * (3x10^8 m/s)^2 = 9x10^16 J, i.e. about 10^17 joule. Mass-energy equivalence with m = 1 kg and c = 3x10^8 m/s gives E = 9x10^16 J (8.99x10^16 J with c = 2.998x10^8). To one order of magnitude, 9x10^16 rounds up to 10^17, not down to 10^16 - and in any case 10^16 is not among the options. Distances to the offered orders: 10^17 is within a factor of 1.11, 10^14 is off by a factor of 900. Answer 10^17 joule.]

stem: Which of the following phenomena cannot take place in sound waves?
solution: Polarisation requires the oscillation to have a direction across the line of travel, so only transverse waves can be polarised. Sound in air is longitudinal - the particles oscillate along the direction of propagation - so there is no transverse direction to restrict and it cannot be polarised. Reflection gives echoes, superposition of two nearby frequencies gives beats, and diffraction is why sound bends round an open doorway, so those three all occur readily. Matches option D.
subject: Physics
subtopic: Sound Behaviours — Reflection, Echo, Reverberation, Beats

stem: The number of electrons contained in 1 coulomb of charge is
solution: Charge is quantised as \(Q = ne\), so the number of electrons is \(n = Q/e = 1/(1.6 \times 10^{-19}) = 6.25 \times 10^{18}\). The tempting last choice is not a count at all - it is the electronic charge itself with the sign of its exponent flipped. Matches option B.
subject: Physics

stem: The refractive indices of glass and water with respect to air are \(\frac{3}{2}\) and \(\frac{4}{3}\) respectively. The refractive index of glass with respect to water will be
solution: The relative refractive index divides one absolute index by the other, so glass with respect to water is \(\frac{3/2}{4/3} = \frac{9}{8}\). The inverted value \(\frac{8}{9}\) is what dividing the wrong way round produces, and it would wrongly imply that light speeds up on passing from water into glass, when glass is the denser medium of the two. Matches option B.
subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR

stem: When a monochromatic light passes from vacuum to a material and vice-versa, which of the following characteristics of the light beam does not change?
solution: Frequency is fixed by the source, and the medium cannot change it: the atoms of the material are driven at the incoming frequency and re-radiate at that same frequency. What does change is the speed, \(v = c/\mu\), and with it the wavelength, since \(\lambda = v/f\); intensity also falls through reflection at the surface and absorption within. Matches option A.

stem: Two wires of the same metal have same length, but their cross-sections are in the ratio 3: 1. They are joined in series. The resistance of thicker wire is 10\(\Omega\). The total resistance of the combination will be
solution: For wires of the same material and the same length, resistance is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section. The thicker wire has three times the area, so if it measures \(10\ \Omega\) the thinner one measures \(30\ \Omega\). Joined in series they add, giving \(10 + 30 = 40\ \Omega\). The trap is reading the 3:1 ratio as a direct proportion, which would wrongly make the thin wire the smaller resistance. Matches option C.

stem: The time period of a simple pendulum is 2 seconds. If its length is increased by 4 times, then its period becomes
solution: For a simple pendulum \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}\), so the period varies as the square root of the length rather than as the length itself. Quadrupling L multiplies T by \(\sqrt{4} = 2\), giving \(2 \times 2 = 4\) seconds. Multiplying the period by 4 instead of by 2 is the slip the longer values reward. Matches option D.

stem: The temperature at which the speed of sound becomes double as was at 27\(^\circ\)C is
solution: In a gas the speed of sound varies as the square root of the absolute temperature, \(v \propto \sqrt{T}\), so doubling the speed needs four times the absolute temperature. Now 27 degrees Celsius is 300 K, so \(T_{2} = 1200\) K, which is \(1200 - 273 = 927\) degrees Celsius. Doubling or quadrupling the Celsius reading instead of the Kelvin reading is what the other values are built on. Matches option C.

stem: At 0 K, which of the following properties of a gas will be zero?
solution: Absolute zero is defined as the temperature at which molecular translational motion ceases, so for an ideal gas the kinetic energy of the molecules becomes zero there. Mass cannot vanish with cooling, density is fixed by mass and volume, and potential energy depends on intermolecular forces rather than on temperature. Matches option A.

stem: Time taken by the sunlight to pass through a glass 3 window of thickness 4 mm whose refractive index is \(\frac{3}{2}\), is
reviewNote: [BROKEN-STEM: Printed defect: a stray digit 3 sits in the stem, which reads "a glass 3 window". No datum is lost or altered - thickness and refractive index are both given cleanly - so the question is answerable as printed. Left as printed.]
solution: Light slows inside the glass to \(v = c/\mu = (3 \times 10^{8})/1.5 = 2 \times 10^{8}\) m/s. Crossing a thickness of \(4 \times 10^{-3}\) m at that speed takes \(t = (4 \times 10^{-3})/(2 \times 10^{8}) = 2 \times 10^{-11}\) s. Using the vacuum speed instead of the reduced speed, or dividing the two the wrong way round, produces the other magnitudes offered. Matches option C.

stem: A ball of mass 2 kg and another of mass 4 kg are dropped together from a 60 feet tall building. After a fall of 30 feet each towards earth, their respective kinetic energies will be in the ratio of
solution: Both balls fall the same 30 feet, and in free fall the speed reached after a given drop is the same whatever the mass, since \(v^{2} = 2gh\) contains no mass. The kinetic energy \(\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\) therefore differs only through the mass, giving \(2 : 4\), that is \(1 : 2\). The same result follows from noting that the kinetic energy equals the potential energy lost, mgh, which is again proportional to mass alone. Matches option D.

stem: Recently superconductivity has been observed at 95K. This temperature is approximately equivalent to

solution: Convert to Celsius first: \(95 - 273 = -178\) degrees Celsius. Then apply \(\frac{9}{5} \times (-178) + 32 = -320.4 + 32 = -288.4\), so the reading is about \(-288\) degrees Fahrenheit. The tempting wrong value is the one quoting \(+178\), which is simply the Celsius figure with its minus sign dropped and its unit left unchanged - and a superconducting transition is certainly not at a temperature well above the boiling point of water. Matches option C.

stem: When a wire is stretched and its radius become \(\frac{r}{2}\) its resistance will be
solution: Stretching conserves the volume of the wire. Halving the radius quarters the area of cross-section, so the length must become four times as great. Since resistance grows in proportion to length and falls in inverse proportion to area, it changes by a factor of \(4 \div \frac{1}{4} = 16\), giving 16R. The common slip is to account for the change in area but forget that the wire must also lengthen, which badly understates the factor. Matches option D.

stem: The temperature of sun can be found out by using
solution: Wien's displacement law, \(\lambda_{m}T = b\), ties the wavelength at which a hot body radiates most strongly to its absolute temperature, so measuring where the solar spectrum peaks yields a surface temperature of about 5800 K directly. This is the standard method for the Sun and for stars generally, whose size and total output cannot be measured as easily. Stefan's law is the tempting alternative, but on its own it gives the total power radiated rather than a temperature, and inverting it needs the Sun's luminosity and radius as well. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following statements is not true?
optA: The resistance of intrinsic semiconductors decreases with increase of temperature.
optB: Doping pure Si with trivalent impurity gives p-type semiconductors.
optC: The majority carriers in n-type semiconductors are holes.
optD: A \(p - n\) junction can act as a semiconductor diode.
solution: In an n-type semiconductor the pentavalent dopant donates one extra electron per atom, so electrons are the majority carriers and holes only the minority ones - the statement claiming holes is therefore the untrue one. The other three are sound: heating an intrinsic semiconductor frees more electron-hole pairs so its resistance falls, a trivalent dopant creates holes and gives p-type material, and a p-n junction is exactly what a semiconductor diode is. Matches option C.

stem: The vitamins, which are generally excreted in urine are
solution: Water-soluble vitamins are not stored in the body, so whatever the tissues do not use is filtered out by the kidneys and passed in the urine, which is why they must be supplied in the diet regularly. The B-complex group and ascorbic acid are the water-soluble ones. Retinol, calciferol and phylloquinone are fat-soluble and are stored in the liver and adipose tissue instead, so they are not routinely excreted. Matches option B.

stem:
Deficiency of which of the following elements is responsible for weakening of bones?
1. Calcium
2. Phosphorus
3. Nitrogen
4. Carbon
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Bone is largely a matrix of calcium phosphate, so a shortage of either calcium or phosphorus weakens the skeleton - as in rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults. Nitrogen and carbon are constituents of every organic molecule in the body and arrive automatically with protein and carbohydrate, so they are never described as deficient in this sense. Matches option A.
subject: Biology

stem: Which one among the following animal tissues transports hormones and maintains water balance?
solution: Blood is a fluid connective tissue, and it is the plasma that carries hormones from the endocrine glands to their target organs and that maintains the body's water and electrolyte balance. Areolar tissue is the tempting distractor because it too is connective, but it packs and binds organs together rather than transporting anything. Muscular tissue contracts and nervous tissue conducts impulses, so neither has a transport role. Matches option A.
subject: Biology

stem: Which of the following structures of a plant is responsible for transpiration?
solution: Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, and about nine-tenths of it passes through the stomata, whose guard cells open and close the pores according to their turgor. Xylem delivers water up to the leaf and phloem carries food, while bark and cuticle exist to restrict water loss rather than to permit it. Matches option C.

stem: Cinnabar is an ore of
solution: Cinnabar is mercuric sulphide, HgS, the chief ore of mercury; roasting it in air gives the free metal directly, which is unusual among sulphide ores. Copper's principal ore is copper pyrites, nickel's is pentlandite, and tungsten's is wolframite. Matches option C.

stem: Wavelength of visible light, X -- rays and microwaves are represented by \(\lambda_{v}\) , \(\lambda_{x}\) and \(\lambda_{m}\) and respectively, then
solution: Across the electromagnetic spectrum wavelength falls as frequency rises. Microwaves run from about a metre down to a millimetre, visible light is a few hundred nanometres, and X-rays are of the order of a tenth of a nanometre. The microwave wavelength is therefore the longest and the X-ray wavelength the shortest, giving \(\lambda_{m} > \lambda_{v} > \lambda_{x}\). Matches option D.

stem: An object weight 10N in air, when immersed fully in a liquid, its weight 8N. The weight of liquid displaced by the object will be
solution: By Archimedes' principle the apparent loss of weight on immersion equals the weight of the fluid displaced. The object loses \(10 - 8 = 2\) N, so the liquid it displaces weighs 2 N. The figure of 8 N is the apparent weight that remains in the liquid, not the buoyant force, and quoting it is the usual error here. Matches option A.

stem: Source of sun's energy is
reviewNote: [BROKEN-STEM: Printed defect: the choices are lettered while the third of them reads "both (1) and (2)", referring to numbered items that do not appear. Its meaning is nonetheless unambiguous - it offers both processes together - and it is a distractor rather than the answer, so the question is answerable as printed. Left as printed.]
solution: The Sun is powered by nuclear fusion: in its core, at a temperature of some 15 million kelvin, hydrogen nuclei fuse through the proton-proton chain into helium, and the small mass difference is released as energy. Fission requires heavy nuclei such as uranium, which the Sun does not possess in any useful quantity, so the choice combining the two processes fails for the same reason as fission alone. Matches option B.

stem: Two resistances of 10\(\Omega\) are parallely connected in a circuit. Equivalent resistance of the circuit will be.
solution: For two resistors in parallel \(\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{2}{10}\), so \(R = 5\ \Omega\). Equal resistors in parallel always give the common value divided by how many there are, and the result must be smaller than either resistor on its own - which rules out the three larger figures immediately. Matches option B.

stem: "Good emitters are good absorbers." This statement is based on
reviewNote: Source typo: option (C) 'Principal of preevost' (for 'Principle of Prevost').
solution: Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation states that at a given temperature and wavelength the emissivity of a surface equals its absorptivity, so a good emitter is necessarily a good absorber. That is why a matt black surface both absorbs and radiates strongly while a polished one does neither. Prevost's theory says only that a body goes on radiating whatever its surroundings, and Stefan's law fixes how the amount radiated grows with temperature; neither equates emission with absorption. Matches option D.
